html:
The Banyjima, also written Panyjima, are an Aboriginal people of the Pilbara in Western Australia, whose country is the Hamersley Range and its deep gorges, now Karijini National Park.

Their neighbours on the map were the Kurrama and Yinhawangka to the west, the Palyku to the east and the Nyamal to the north. The gorges held permanent water, and people moved between them and the plains with the seasons.

In the 1900s their country was changed by mining. Blue asbestos was mined at Wittenoom from the 1930s to 1966, leaving a deadly legacy, and from the 1960s huge iron ore mines opened in the Hamersleys. Banyjima people now share in the management of Karijini. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Banyjima, also written Panyjima, are an Aboriginal people of the Pilbara in Western Australia, whose country is the Hamersley Range and its deep gorges, now Karijini National Park.
